newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Beijing top office space see more demand-surveyor.
newsitem.headline: Beijing top office space see more demand-surveyor.

text.p: An independent property surveyor said on Tuesday the price of prime office space in Beijing was expected to rise in coming years due to strong demand.

Leung Chun-ying, managing director of C.Y. Leung & Company Ltd, cited tight land supply and the continued influx of multinational companies into Beijing as main factors for the company's bullish outlook in its newly-launched report, Property Times.
Growth in capital values of Beijing's prime office premises topped other major Chinese cities such as Shanghai, Guangzhou and Shenzhen, it said.

Sales prices for Grade A office buildings in Beijing have gone up by 52.3 percent since 1993, while those in Shanghai, Guangzhou and Shenzhen have risen by 15.7 percent, 9.4 percent and 0.4 percent respectively, it said.
Its Beijing office rental index however has been on a downward trend since the fourth quarter of 1994 amid an increase in office supply during the period.
The phenomenon showed that investors were more receptive towards a longer payback period, Leung expained.
